Priya Nair: Escalating a Private deployment security/compliance issue from MedicoSys. They report repeated API 500s and KMS "AccessDenied" errors for model request decrypts. Compliance asking for audit log retention proof. Can eng-security triage? Ticket #SUP-56421
Tom Rivers: Copy. Do we have repro steps from support? Any specific KMS key ARN or HSM details?
Priya Nair: Customer shared these quick repro steps and logs:

1) POST to our hosted endpoint via their VPC NAT (private deployment)
2) Logs: `2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR decrypt: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to use the key` (full stack attached in ticket)
3) They show backend latency spikes ~ 2.1s per call when retries occur
4) They say outbound egress policy blocks port 443 except to allowed FQDNs and they only allow a small set of external IPs

They want: (a) confirmation we don't persist payloads longer than our retention policy, (b) audit logs proving key usage, (c) advice to open minimal ports/rules so KMS/HSM calls don't fail.
Asha Gupta: Thanks. Quick note: Private deployments call Redwood KMS proxy endpoints over TLS from inside customer VPC via configured egress. If egress blocks TLS to our KMS endpoint IP ranges, you'll get AccessDenied? OR timeout depending on intercept. Need to check whether their request even reaches KMS. Can they share tcpdump or fw logs?
Devon Li: Priority check: if traffic is being NATed through enterprise firewall with TLS inspection, that can break client certificate pinning for HSM connections. Also HSMs (if configured in customer region) use mTLS to our control plane — failing mTLS can surface as auth errors.
Maya Chen: I pulled the initial packet capture support attached in SUP-56421. Quick grep shows TLS handshake failures to our kms-proxy: `alert TLSv1.3 HANDSHAKE FAILURE ciphersuite` and `server hello read: unknown certificate` around the same timestamps as decrypt errors. Here's the relevant excerpt:

```
14:02:09.752 IP 10.0.3.45.443 > 172.31.12.8.50732: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 229, length 511
TLSv1.3 Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Server Hello (encrypted)
14:02:09.754 TLSv1.3 Alert: Handshake Failure
```

Tom Rivers: That points at TLS interception. Action items: ask customer to temporarily allow direct egress to redwood-kms.*.redwood-inference.com on 443 from service subnets (no TLS MITM) and/or provide a host-level curl inside their runtime container to our kms endpoint to confirm behavior.
Priya Nair: Customer tried `curl -v https://kms-proxy.redwood-inference.com/decrypt` from their runtime container and saw `SSL: certificate verify failed` + HTTP 403 eventually.
Asha Gupta: 403 + cert verify fail is consistent with outbound proxy doing TLS interception and replacing cert chain. For mTLS-protected HSM calls, that will break. Suggested minimal rule set:
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to kms-proxy.redwood-inference.com (FQDN) and to the region-specific HSM endpoint(s)
- Allow outbound UDP/ICMP as required for path MTU and DNS
- Do not perform TLS MITM on connections to our KMS/HSM endpoints

Devon Li: Also verify egress SNAT IPs in customer firewall. Our KMS ACL expects requests from their registered SNAT ranges when customer uses private KMS key policies. If SNATs changed, that can cause AccessDenied on key policy checks.
Priya Nair: Compliance question: they asked how long we retain request logs and what is in the audit logs. Can we provide a canonical statement and what artifacts we can share?
Maya Chen: From platform side: we keep operational request traces for 90 days by default, and sanitized audit logs (no customer prompt text) for 365 days for enterprise plans — but I need eng-security sign-off on what we can share with customers. We can provide a signed snippet of CloudTrail-style events for KMS: `Decrypt` calls, source IP, timestamp, key ARN, and operation result. We do NOT include decrypted plaintext.
Tom Rivers: Confirming: we can export KMS operation events (key usage) and service-side audit events. For Private deployments, the customer's private control plane also exports local audit logs — ask customer to attach their control plane logs for cross-correlation. We should also redact any user prompt content before sharing.
Priya Nair: Customer also flagged billing: they saw retries generating higher token usage. They want advice to avoid retries causing double billing.
Asha Gupta: Recommend exponential backoff + idempotency token in request metadata. Also suggest configuring local 429/503 fallback to a cheaper local cached embedding when model decrypt fails. We can provide code snippet for client-side retries.
Maya Chen: Quick repro I ran in a sandbox container using their exact egress rules: when TLS interception is present, KMS decrypt fails with status 403 and `AccessDenied` in the service logs. When I allowed direct egress to kms-proxy and disabled interception, calls succeed and decrypt latency drops to ~40ms.

```
# inside container
curl -i -sS https://kms-proxy.redwood-inference.com/health
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","version":"2026-02-12"}
```

Devon Li: Next steps for eng-security:
- [ ] Verify what artifacts we can release to the customer for compliance (audit event samples, signed statements)
- [ ] Produce a one-pager minimal egress firewall rules + SNAT guidance for Private deployments
- [ ] Confirm whether HSM mTLS failure surfaces as AccessDenied vs timeout (add to troubleshooting doc)
